public_rationale: Anthropic's June 4, 2026 report describes AI assistance with development and explicitly says fully autonomous successor development has not been reached [e1]. Its April 2026 research account describes agents proposing ideas, running experiments and analyzing results within a supplied research problem [e2]. The central distinction holds, although 'coding tool' understates the research activities demonstrated within assigned tasks [e1, e2].
limitations: The evidence concerns disclosed work and does not establish undisclosed capabilities.
Working within a human-assigned research problem does not imply human approval of every action [e2].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: What Anthropic has shown is a useful human-leveraged coding tool good at some code optimizations, not actual recursive self-improvement, which remains speculative.

statement.excerpt: RSI would be “an AI system capable of fully autonomously designing and developing its own successor” but what’s been shown us so far a useful coding tool that humans can leverag; it’s great for example at (some) code optimizations, but not even (as the blog makes clear) actual RSI, which remains speculative.

our_interpretation: Assess the results disclosed in Anthropic's June 4 blog, not undisclosed research.

criteria.support_condition: The report describes useful development assistance and optimization under essential human direction, without demonstrating fully autonomous successor design and development.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The report demonstrates a system fully autonomously designing and developing its successor, or establishes that the reported work did not depend on essential human direction.
